notes: Check batch 2026-10-29-check for order-report: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and model_id matching their tier; each result.json records head 6d3eb7f with uncommitted true and skill_hash ca223baf..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, and every transcript contains the three reworded sentences under test ("with `&1` and `&2` in that order and each used once", "A pipeline never sits on one line", "A `for` always takes"). Haiku-2 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md, the other three SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against a stand-in Decimal written there (no Decimal package is available, which is why compiles carries Decimal warnings). A probe gave correct per-currency totals, last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day in all four), empty results for [] and {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status and a bad date. Haiku-1's top_customers keeps customers with zero completed orders ({"b", 0} in the probe); haiku-1 and haiku-2 report the last order as a DateTime rather than a date; sonnet-1 reports a missing key as :invalid_order and haiku-2 as {:invalid_field, key}; no rule in the list covers these, so they are noted in the summaries only.

Changed rules, graded against the current text. "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else": decided by "Use `do:` for a body of one expression with no body of its own inside it", "A capture that carries a call with arguments of its own ... is a second body too", the if sentence and "A `for` always takes `do ... end`". Every do: body in the four runs is a tuple, a literal or a comparison (parse_status/1 everywhere, sonnet-1's catch-all clauses, completed?/1 in both Sonnet runs); no do: body holds a fn or a capture, and no run writes if or for, so the if and for sentences have no case here. Haiku-2's only capture with its own arguments, &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2), sits in a do ... end body (sum_amounts/1, lines 169-171). The mixed-function sentence is exercised only by sonnet-1 (parse_order/1, parse_amount/1, parse_placed_at/1), each block clause set apart by a blank line. Runs violating: 0 of 4 (previous sweep 0 of 5 under the old wording).

"Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom" is newly listed for order-report, so there is no earlier verdict to compare. The new sentence "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short" decides nothing here: no run puts two or more pipeline steps on one line (0 of 4), and no pipeline starts with a kind or mode argument. Sonnet-2 is violated by the unchanged bullet "Do not pipe a single step: write `String.trim(name)`, not `name |> String.trim()`.": lines 118-119, rows |> Enum.reduce_while({:ok, []}, fn ...). Haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 are clean. Runs violating: 1 of 4.

"Use captures for one-call lambdas and `fn` for anything longer": the new sentence "with `&1` and `&2` in that order and each used once" decides haiku-2 line 170, &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2), as clean; no run passes &2 before &1 or uses a placeholder twice. The other captures are one call or one operator with &1 once (sonnet-2 line 93: &DateTime.to_date(&1.placed_at)). Runs violating: 0 of 4.

"Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" (the trailing keyword list and six-element sentences) is not in order-report's list; no run passes a multi-line literal as an argument or writes a literal of more than six elements (the longest is the five-atom @enforce_keys list), so nothing is listed under it. "Break a `->` clause whose pattern and body together pass 70 characters" is now committed with the same text graded in 2026-10-23-check-3 and is graded to that standard: every one-line clause was measured after its indentation; the longest are 66 (haiku-1 line 74, haiku-2 line 92) and 60 (sonnet-1 line 120, sonnet-2 line 167); no clause passes 70 and none is broken; one-line fn arguments are outside the rule. 0 of 4 violated, 4 of 4 exercised.

Unchanged rules, same standard as 2026-10-23/grades/order-report-skill.json. The with rule: build/1's single parse call is a case in all four (haiku-1 36, haiku-2 57, sonnet-1 66, sonnet-2 75); the withs have eight (haiku-1, sonnet-2), five plus three two-step field helpers (haiku-2) or three steps (sonnet-1), with no else. Enum/Map: 0 of 4; all group with Enum.group_by then Map.new; the Sonnet runs count with frequencies_by while the Haiku runs take Enum.count/length of the filtered list that also feeds the totals, held clean as before; the Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces. Lists: all four prepend in reduce_while without reversing, held clean as before because nothing downstream depends on the order. Naming, dates, money, atoms and processes: all four clean. Sonnet-1's multi-line parse_order/1 head binding the five required keys is held clean under the head rule because a catch-all clause follows it. Outside the list: haiku-1's build/1 @doc has no examples (Comments rule) and its Order struct has no @type t (struct rule), as earlier batches listed the same shapes; haiku-2's two `_ ->` clauses (lines 93, 107) are listed under Match every expected shape, as earlier batches listed Decimal.parse/1 catch-alls. No other violation was found.
